newsitem.title: USA: 3DO targets Internet, to divest hardware.
newsitem.headline: 3DO targets Internet, to divest hardware.

text.p: 3DO Co said on Monday it will restructure to focus entirely on the Internet and game entertainment software, and will sell its 3DO systems hardware business or turn it into a joint venture.

In the reorganization, 3DO President Hugh Martin will assume full operating control of the company, 3DO said. Trip Hawkins remains chairman and chief executive but will shift his focus to the role of creative director.
"The Internet, and Internet entertainment in particular, is a huge opportunity," Hawkins said in a statement. 3DO will launch its first Internet-specific product on Tuesday.
The product, called Meridian 59, is a multi-user game that can be played over the Internet. In early, free trials of the game, 3DO has signed up over 25,000 accounts.

The move represents a nearly complete circle for 3DO since going public in a highly publicized 1993 stock offering that saw its stock shoot skyward based largely on expectations for the technologically advanced 3DO game player.

When video game machines from industry stalwarts like Sega Enterprises Ltd and Nintendo caught up to 3DO's technology, however, 3DO's sales began to lag. And it never captured the market share analysts, investors and the company wanted.

Last year, Matsushita Industrial Electric Co Ltd paid 3DO $100 million to license its technology and build an new generation of game players, called "M2". At that time, 3DO said it would concentrate on developing games and software.
"We are moving toward focusing entirely on the challenge of building a strong entertainment software studio, with the Internet as a catalyst for growth," Hawkins said.

When the game player unit is sold or spun off to a joint venture, 3DO will employ about 300 people, down from 450 currently. The company said it could not predict the timing or financial effects of a possible deal.
3DO added, however, it is currently exploring partnering opportunities with several companies and expects to complete a joint venture or sale of the hardware business by year end.
In the reorganization, software product development will be reorganized into five production units, the largest of which will be the Internet group.
Studio 3DO will be reorganized into two units. The other two units are Cyclone Studios and New World Computing, both acquired in the last year.

As part of the reorganization, the company has taken steps to reduce its cash consumption rate by eliminating entertainment projects with outside developers and reassigning internal staff to its most promising software titles.
Following the announcement, 3DO's stock dropped 1-5/16 to 6-13/16.
